signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: In the second quarter, sales and revenues were better than expected at $20.5 billion, up 24% versus the prior year, driven by strong end market demand in all three of our primary segments.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: This milestone underscores both the essential work our customers do every day and the dedication of Caterpillar employees worldwide to solving our customers' toughest challenges.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Our backlog grew sequentially by $9 billion to $72 billion.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Strong order rates and a growing backlog reflect broadening momentum across our business.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: In the quarter, we generated robust MP&E free cash flow of $5.1 billion and deployed $2.2 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: As I mentioned, sales and revenues were $20.5 billion, and the increase versus prior year was primarily driven by strong growth in sales volume from higher sales to users in all three primary segments and favorable price realization.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Second quarter sales and revenues were better than expected due to strong sales volume growth in Construction Industries and Resource Industries, while Power & Energy was broadly in line with our expectations.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Second quarter adjusted operating profit margin was better than we anticipated, primarily due to IEEPA tariff recoveries of $392 million and lower-than-expected tariff costs.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: The margin benefit from better-than-expected sales volume was mostly offset by higher SG&A and R&D expense.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: For tariffs introduced since the beginning of 2025, excluding IEEPA recoveries, costs were about $400 million in the quarter.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Sales to users grew in all three of our primary segments.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: In Power & Energy, sales to users grew a robust 33%.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Power generation grew 72%, driven by very strong demand for large gensets and turbines used in data center applications.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Sales to users in oil and gas increased 6% and were driven by reciprocating engines, turbines and turbine-related services sold into gas compression applications.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Industrial sales to users were down due to a decline in engines sold in the marine application.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Construction Industries total sales to users grew for the sixth consecutive quarter, up 22%.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Increases in North America were better than we anticipated as the growth was driven by very strong rental fleet loading and equipment sold into nonresidential and residential construction.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Dealers' rental revenue continues to grow in North America, requiring more investment in their equipment fleets.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: This quarter, rental loading was a positive contributor to sales to user growth as compared to second quarter last year when rental loading was a headwind.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Sales to users increased in EAME due to strength in Europe and Africa, but were lower than we anticipated due to softness in the Middle East.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: In Asia Pacific, growth was driven by China, but softness outside of China kept the overall region below our expectations.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Latin America grew as we anticipated.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: For Resource Industries, second quarter sales to users increased 17%, which was in line with our expectations.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: To support the demand growth in power generation and oil and gas applications, we're excited to resume production of our 10-megawatt medium-speed gas reciprocating engine platform.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: And now without significant investment, we're able to restart production by leveraging our existing supply base along with our internal capacity and capability.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: And finally, Resource Industries completed the acquisition of Skycatch in July, further enhancing our capabilities following the recent acquisition of RPMGlobal.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: That allows customers to identify, measure and interact with the data, resulting in improved decision-making, reduced delays and greater confidence in daily operations.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: This is another example of investment in technology-enabled growth that will help our mining customers operate more efficiently and achieve better outcomes.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We continue to see strong momentum in our end markets despite ongoing uncertainty due to geopolitical events.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We are increasing our full year 2026 sales and revenues expectations to mid- to high-teens growth based on the healthy demand we are seeing across all three of our primary segments.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: As a result, we anticipate stronger full year growth across all three primary segments compared to the outlook we gave in April.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Services revenues are also expected to grow at a higher rate for the full year compared to our previous outlook.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: The improved outlook is also supported by the breadth and duration of our record backlog.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Currently, 59% of our $72 billion backlog is expected to be delivered over the next 12 months.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: This percentage has been fairly stable over the past three quarters, which demonstrates the momentum in all three primary segments.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We expect the full year adjusted operating profit margin to be higher than we expected during our last earnings call, reflecting the improved sales and revenues outlook.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Excluding the favorable impact from our IEEPA tariff recoveries in the second quarter, we expect full year adjusted operating profit margin to be near the bottom of the target range.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Our full year margin expectation reflects the strategic investments we are making to execute our growth strategy as well as the ongoing impact of tariffs.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: While the situation around tariffs remains fluid, we continue to execute our mitigation plans.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Kyle will provide more detail on our revised full year estimate for tariffs in a moment.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: I'm confident that we'll manage the impact of tariffs over time as we aim to operate around the midpoint of our adjusted operating profit margin target range.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We are also increasing our MP&E free cash flow expectations to be in the top half of our annual target range, reflecting our improved outlook.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Our positive outlook for 2026 continues to reflect strong demand in power generation and oil and gas.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Strong second quarter performance has set a solid foundation for continued growth for the remainder of the year.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We continue to anticipate full year growth in power generation for both Cat reciprocating engines and Solar Turbines driven by increasing energy demand to support data center build-out related to cloud computing and generative AI.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: After a record year for sales in 2025, oil and gas is expected to grow moderately again this year.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Reciprocating engine sales are anticipated to increase driven by strong demand in gas compression applications.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We also see continued momentum in demand for reciprocating engine aftermarket parts.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Solar Turbines oil and gas sales are expected to grow while the backlog remains healthy, as we continue to see solid order and inquiry activity.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Demand for products in industrial applications is expected to grow moderately in 2026.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: For Construction Industries, we continue to expect full year sales to users growth, supported by strong order rates.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Overall, the outlook for North America remains positive as sales to users are anticipated to grow versus last year.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Nonresidential investment in critical infrastructure programs, heavy construction and data centers is contributing to overall construction spending levels.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We expect dealer rental fleet loading will continue to grow including additional fleet loading for Major Projects in the third quarter.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: While the Middle East continues to be challenged, we currently anticipate only a limited impact on EAME sales to users.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: In Asia Pacific outside of China, softer economic conditions are expected.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: In China, we anticipate moderate conditions with full year growth in the above 10-ton excavator industry off of low levels of activity.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We expect full year growth in Latin America.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: We're seeing continued positive momentum in Resource Industries with robust order rates and strong backlog growth.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: For 2026, sales to users are expected to increase, primarily driven by rising demand for copper and gold and positive dynamics in heavy construction and quarry and aggregates.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Most key commodities remain above investment thresholds.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Rail services and locomotive deliveries are both anticipated to grow for the year.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: As we invest in our capacity to meet customers' increasing needs, we're finding creative ways to reallocate resources and optimize our operations as we grow to record levels.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Last November, we announced an increase in our new turbine capacity of 2.5x 2024 levels.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: This capacity will serve oil and gas and power generation applications and be leveraged to provide rebuild and services for our growing installed base for decades to come.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: From Wamego, we now package and ship our PGM130, a product that is popular for data center power generation.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: This is one of many examples of how we are continuing to manage our business with discipline and maximize the use of our existing footprint to serve our customers and grow profitably.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Sales and revenues were $20.5 billion, up 24% versus the prior year, which was better than our expectations.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Adjusted operating profit was $4.5 billion, and our adjusted operating profit margin was 21.9%, both better than we anticipated.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The 24% increase in sales and revenues compared to the second quarter of 2025 was primarily driven by strong growth in sales volume and favorable price realization.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The stronger sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users across all three primary segments.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Dealer inventory increased by $400 million in Construction Industries compared to a decrease in the second quarter of 2025.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The increase was higher than we originally anticipated, supported by our expectation of stronger sales to users for the rest of the year, which reflects strong end market demand.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Sales and revenues were above our expectations, mainly driven by stronger-than-expected sales volume in Construction Industries and Resource Industries.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Operating profit in the second quarter increased by 50% to $4.3 billion.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Adjusted operating profit of $4.5 billion increased by 54% versus the prior year, mainly due to the profit impact of higher sales volume.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Margin was better than we anticipated, primarily due to expected IEEPA tariff recoveries and lower-than-expected tariff costs.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The margin benefit from better-than-expected sales volume was mostly offset by higher SG&A and R&D expense.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In the quarter, we recognized $392 million in expected IEEPA tariff recoveries with the majority of this amount reflected in corporate items.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: For the tariffs introduced since the beginning of 2025, excluding IEEPA recoveries, the second quarter tariff costs were approximately $400 million.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: This favorability was primarily driven by adjustments to the computation of tariffs previously incurred.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The $400 million of tariff costs were recognized within the segments and corporate items.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Restructuring costs in the quarter were $0.40 versus $0.10 last year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Finally, the year-over-year impact from the reduction in the average number of shares outstanding due to share repurchases resulted in a favorable impact on adjusted profit per share of approximately $0.15 compared to the second quarter of 2025.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: On Slide 11, I will now review the second quarter performance of the segments, starting with Power & Energy.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: For Power & Energy, sales of $8.2 billion increased by 17% versus the prior year, which was generally in line with our expectations.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The sales increase versus the prior year was mainly due to higher sales volume and favorable price realization.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Second quarter profit for Power & Energy increased by 30% versus the prior year to $2 billion.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The increase was mainly due to the profit impact of higher sales volume and favorable price realization, which was partially offset by unfavorable manufacturing costs.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Segment margin was higher than anticipated, primarily due to lower-than-expected manufacturing costs, including tariffs.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Construction Industries sales increased by 35% in the second quarter to $8.3 billion, primarily due to higher sales volume and favorable price realization.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The $400 million of dealer inventory increase and services revenue growth resulted in sales volume to be better than we expected.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Resource Industries sales increased by 20% in the second quarter to $4.6 billion, primarily driven by higher sales volume.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Sales were better than we anticipated due to higher sales volume, driven by favorable services revenues growth.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Second quarter profit for Resource Industries increased by 23% versus the prior year to $693 million.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Financial Products revenues increased by 10% versus the prior year to $1.1 billion, mainly due to higher average earning assets across all regions.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Segment profit increased by 32% to $328 million.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Our customers' financial health remains strong.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Retail new business volume grew by 9% versus the prior year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: MP&E free cash flow was a record at $5.1 billion in the second quarter.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: This was about $2.8 billion increase versus the prior year, mainly driven by stronger profit.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We deployed $2.2 billion to shareholders in the second quarter.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Share repurchases accounted for about $1.5 billion, with the remainder reflecting our quarterly dividend payment.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In June, we announced an 8% dividend increase, our sixth consecutive year with a high single-digit quarterly increase.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We are continuing to monitor the environment as geopolitical conditions remain fluid and complex.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Based on what we see today for the third quarter, we anticipate another strong quarter of sales growth versus the prior year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We expect volume increases and favorable price realization in each of our three primary segments.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We anticipate volume growth will be driven by higher sales to users across all three primary segments versus the prior year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: If we look at the segments, we anticipate strong sales growth in Power & Energy in the third quarter versus the prior year, driven by continued strength in power generation and in oil and gas, modest growth in industrial applications as it continues to recover and favorable price realization.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In Construction Industries, we expect strong sales growth in the third quarter versus the prior year mainly due to higher sales volume on strong sales to users and favorable price realization.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: As a result, the year-over-year impact from dealer inventory is expected to be a modest headwind to sales volume in the quarter.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In Resource Industries, we also expect strong sales growth in the third quarter versus the prior year primarily due to higher sales to users and services growth.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Now I will provide some color on our third quarter margin expectations versus the prior year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We expect higher adjusted operating profit margin at the enterprise level versus prior year, primarily due to favorable price realization and higher sales volume, partially offset by unfavorable manufacturing cost including depreciation expense and freight, along with higher SG&A and R&D expenses due to the continued investment in strategic investments aligned with our 2030 goals that we rolled out at our last year's Investor Day.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We anticipate tariff costs of around $600 million, which is similar to what we incurred in the third quarter of 2025.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We expect about 50% of the tariffs to be incurred in Construction Industries and 25% in both Power & Energy and Resource Industries.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In Power & Energy, we anticipate a higher margin percentage compared to the prior year on stronger volume and favorable price realization.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: SG&A and R&D expenses are also expected to be higher.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In Construction Industries, we anticipate a higher margin percentage compared to the prior year, primarily due to favorable price realization and higher sales volume.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Strategic investments related to technology are expected to increase SG&A and R&D expenses versus prior year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In Resource Industries, we anticipate a similar margin percentage compared to the prior year due to higher sales volume and favorable price realization, partially offset by higher manufacturing costs, including tariff costs and SG&A and R&D expenses.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: As Joe mentioned, we now anticipate sales and revenues growth in the mid- to high-teens for the full year of 2026.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: The increase in our full year sales and revenue expectations is supported by strong sales to users growth across all three primary segments driven by healthy end markets, strong order rates across all three primary segments driving backlog growth and increased throughput from our capacity expansion plans in the second half.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We expect strong sales growth across each of our primary segments, mainly driven by volume and price.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: For the enterprise, we typically see higher sales and revenues in the second half as compared to the first, and we expect to follow that trend this year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We plan to end the year higher than last year in anticipation of future end market growth.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: As a result, the year-over-year impact from dealer inventory is expected to be a headwind to Construction Industries sales volume in the second half of the year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Now on to adjusted operating profit margin for the full year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Due to the increased sales and revenues outlook, full year adjusted operating profit margin will be higher than we expected in April.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Excluding the expected IEEPA tariff recoveries, our full year adjusted operating margin would be near the bottom of the range at the higher sales level.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Compared to last year, higher adjusted operating profit margin will reflect favorable price realization, higher sales volume, partially offset by higher manufacturing costs, including tariffs, depreciation expense and freight and higher SG&A and R&D, driven by compensation expense and strategic investments spend.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Excluding the expected IEEPA tariff recoveries of approximately $400 million reported in the second quarter, we now expect full year 2026 tariff costs of around $2.2 billion or at the low end of the range we previously provided.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Our outlook does not include any additional IEEPA tariff recoveries in the second half of the year.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: As we lap incremental tariff costs, the tariff impact to the second half adjusted operating profit and margins is not expected to be significant.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We continue to expect restructuring costs of approximately $300 million to $350 million in 2026.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: With the improved sales and revenues and adjusted operating margin outlook, we now expect MP&E free cash flow to be in the top half of our annual target range of $6 billion to $15 billion.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We expect second half MP&E free cash flow to be slightly higher than the first half despite higher CapEx spend.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We delivered a strong first half with better-than-expected sales and revenues and earnings.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: In this dynamic operating environment, we now anticipate mid- to high-teens sales and revenues growth in 2026 and anticipate adjusted operating profit margin and MP&E free cash flow to be better than we had previously expected.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We remain disciplined and committed to operational excellence and the O&E model.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We will continue to look for ways to optimize our footprint and invest efficiently.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: We are maintaining a strong balance sheet, and we will continue to return substantially all of our MP&E free cash flow to our shareholders through dividends and share repurchases over time.

signals.speaker: Kyle Epley
signals.sentence: Finally, we will continue to execute our strategy for profitable growth.

signals.sentence: Customers, I don't think, are going to rush to Cat dealers for our equipment if they can't also get the other rental equipment that they need.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: Major Projects fleet really allows us - it's a national fleet and allows us to move that fleet around to really supplement dealers where if a dealer has a major infrastructure project in their territory for a couple of years or three years, it's tough for them to invest in the fleet that size to keep up at that scale or knowing that that job may be somewhere else a few years from now.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: That Major Projects fleet is going to really help us supplement the dealers, which should allow them also to grow because they'll be the ones that are working on that project in a local territory, and then we'll use the Major Projects fleet to supplement their existing fleet.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: I'm really proud of our team and the record performance this quarter.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: In particular, the sales and revenues milestone we achieved - the first time in our company history to exceed $20 billion in the quarter.

signals.speaker: Joseph Creed
signals.sentence: With broadening momentum across all three of our primary segments, we'll remain focused on operational excellence and delivering for our customers to create long-term value for our shareholders.
